summary: Popup Image MongoDB Migration hotfix VERIFIED end-to-end. Backend pytest 6/6 PASS (upload writes doc to db.popup_images w/ base64 data + width=800/height=450/content_type=image/jpeg + 32-char hex image_id; public GET /api/popup-image/{id} returns 200 w/ real JPEG bytes matching upload size WITHOUT any Authorization header — the critical browser use-case; nonexistent id → 404; no auth = 401; regular user token = 403; create+active-fetch round-trip returns the /api/popup-image/{id} URL intact). Frontend E2E via Playwright: admin login → /admin/popup-messages → New Popup → image upload → Live Preview shows the image (data-testid='admin-popup-image-preview', src=https://…/api/popup-image/, naturalWidth=800, naturalHeight=450) → Save. Logged out and back in as test user (9970100782/997010) → popup rendered with image visible (naturalWidth=800, naturalHeight=450 → confirms image successfully loaded, not broken). All 3 close escape hatches verified: × close button, backdrop click (with fresh sessionStorage), ESC key press. Regression: legacy /api/static/popups/xxx.jpg URLs return 404 but frontend renders `` tag with no crash (no onError needed — browser handles gracefully).

minor.issue: Cache-Control header 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable' set by handler but overridden by upstream middleware to 'no-store' (documented as known/acceptable in review request). Image still loads correctly; only client caching is disabled. Low priority — can revisit.

action_items: OPTIONAL: consider adding onError={(e)=>{e.currentTarget.style.display='none'}} on to avoid broken-image icon for legacy /api/static/popups/*.jpg records that still exist in DB but files were wiped. Current behavior is browser-default (blank space), which is acceptable but not polished.

OPTIONAL: response payload of /upload-image also returns 'compression_ratio' — for tiny source PNGs (e.g. 400x300 solid) this can be a negative percentage since PNG (7KB) → JPEG 800x450 (88KB) is a growth, not shrink. Consider clamping/labeling appropriately, or drop the field to avoid confusing UX in admin panel.
critical_code_review_comments: admin_popup_routes.py L437: hard-coded `/api/popup-image/{image_id}` string in response — good, matches server.py wiring at L37188. Any future refactor of the api_router prefix must update BOTH the handler string and the router mount to stay consistent.

admin_popup_routes.py L446 `get_popup_image` is a **public** endpoint by design — confirmed working w/ no auth header. Ensure no future auth middleware is applied to `public_router` (it currently has no auth deps and inherits nothing from admin_popup_router).

admin_popup_routes.py L453 projection `{'_id': 0, 'data_b64': 1, 'content_type': 1}` mixes exclusion (_id) with inclusion — MongoDB accepts this special case for _id but flagging for reviewer awareness. Works today.
PopupMessage.js L136-143: `` has no `onError` handler. If image_url points to a deleted resource, browser will show broken-image icon. Add gracefully hide-on-error for robustness (see action_items).

admin_popup_routes.py L378: 5 MB limit check happens AFTER file.read() — for adversarial 5 GB uploads this could DoS RAM. Consider streaming/size-check via `file.size` or Content-Length header before read. Low priority given upstream ingress limits.

rca of the issue: Original prod bug: popup images stored on local disk (backend/static/popups/) — Emergent containers have ephemeral storage → files wiped on redeploy/restart → end-user tags 404 while admin preview (in-memory session) still displayed the image. Fix migrates storage to db.popup_images (base64 in MongoDB, guaranteed cross-pod + cross-restart persistence) with a new PUBLIC /api/popup-image/{id} endpoint (browser tags need no auth header). Verified end-to-end: upload persists to Mongo, public fetch returns real JPEG bytes matching upload size, end-user browser renders the image with naturalWidth=800/naturalHeight=450 (proves successful decode, not broken).
